subject: Private VPC deployment options and networking follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC follow-up and next steps (Acme Retail)

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a couple action items so we stay aligned: 

Summary of your requirements:
- Production-grade inference for customer-facing features (~200 rps peak; 20–40 ms target p50 token latency)
- Hard requirement: data never leaves your VPC; must support private connectivity for inference requests
- Security team wants options evaluated: AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint) vs VPC Peering + IP allowlist.
- Expected timeline: Prod pilot in Q4, broader rollout in Q1.

Open items / asks for your team:
1) Can you confirm whether Acme prefers PrivateLink (managed endpoint) or VPC peering? Security has a preference but we want to validate technical constraints.
2) Approximate list of CIDR ranges or expected egress IPs you can allowlist (or if you prefer PrivateLink, we’ll provide the VPCE service name).
3) Any compliance artifacts your security team needs up front (SOC2 type II, KMS/HSM notes)—I can loop in our security lead.

I attached a short Private VPC checklist that outlines the connectivity options, required IAM roles, and what we will need from your networking team. I’ve looped in Dylan (solution engineering) to help with the topology options and Sean (solutions lead) who can coordinate the pilot sizing.

Proposed next step: 30-min follow-up with your networking/security folks next week to choose PrivateLink vs peering and confirm allowlist IPs. Is Tue 8/11 or Wed 8/12 better?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0190
Redwood Inference

Attachments: private-vpc-checklist.pdf (1 page - checklist)

From: Alice Park <alice.park@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Security Team <security@ctech.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC follow-up and next steps (Acme Retail)

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and the checklist, that was helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

- Our security team is leaning toward PrivateLink due to their preference for interface endpoints and not having to manage cross-account routing. However, they asked for a short comparison doc that highlights pros/cons for our environment (latency, NAT/egress considerations, and cost).
- In terms of IP allowlisting, our infra team can open a small set of firewall rules if you provide expected egress IPs, but we prefer PrivateLink if it makes the network simpler.
- Compliance: we will need SOC 2 Type II report and a short note on how keys are managed (KMS integration). Please send those to security@ctech.com.

For the follow-up call, Wed 8/12 10:00 AM PT works for us — I’ll send a calendar invite with our networking folks.

Thanks,
Alice Park
Director, Product Engineering
Acme Retail

Alice —

Perfect, thanks for the quick answers and for scheduling Wed 8/12 at 10:00 AM PT. A few notes ahead of the call so we can make the session actionable: 

1) PrivateLink vs VPC peering: attached is a short architecture doc (redwood-private-vpc-architecture.pdf) that compares the two for common patterns. TL;DR: PrivateLink simplifies routing and avoids cross-account route propagation; peering can be lower cost for very high throughput but requires route tables and potential NAT considerations. We’ll run some latency estimates for your 200 rps workload during the call.

2) Egress IPs and allowlist: If you prefer allowlisting, our managed hosted egress IPs (for Dedicated & hosted variants) are published per-region. For Private VPC (VPCE) we provide the service name; there’s no public egress IP to allowlist in that flow. Sean — can you confirm the set of published egress IP ranges we should share if Acme asks for them?

3) Compliance artifacts: looping in our compliance contact; we can provide SOC2 Type II and a summary of our KMS integration before the call. Security@ctech.com — please let us know any specific export controls or additional items you want us to surface.

Action items going into Wed’s call:
- Sean: quick sizing/latency estimate for PrivateLink vs peering for 200 rps target
- Dylan: sample VPC endpoint setup diagram and suggested SG/NACL guidance (I’ve attached a VPCE setup diagram)
- Marissa (me): provide SOC2 + KMS note and a drafted mutual action plan after call

See attached docs: redwood-private-vpc-architecture.pdf, vpce-setup-diagram.pdf

Thanks all — look forward to the call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
